contributions.text: Proposes Saethtior, a test generator for Java that targets surviving mutants, selecting inputs by the mutants they kill.
contributions.quote: First, a generator that targets surviving mutants.

contributions.text: Adds a check that reruns each newly generated test to identify flaky tests, which are reported separately rather than discarded.
contributions.quote: Second, a check that reruns each new test to find flaky ones.

contributions.text: Reports an evaluation on 30 open-source projects, comparing against a random baseline.
contributions.quote: Third, an evaluation on 30 open-source projects.

evaluation.text: Evaluates on 30 Java projects, seeding faults with a different mutation tool than the one used for guidance, under the same ten-minute budget as a random baseline. Reports 18% more seeded faults found and 42 flaky tests, 37 confirmed by hand.
evaluation.quote: we give Saethtior and a random baseline the same ten-minute budget

prior_work.text: Contrasts itself with search-based test generation, which the authors say optimizes coverage rather than using mutants. Cites mutation-analysis studies to motivate using mutants, and fuzzers for sharing input mutation but targeting crashes.
prior_work.quote: Search-based test generation [1] optimizes coverage and does not use mutants.

closest_cited_work.text: The paper's genetic-algorithm search for killing inputs is described as following the style of this earlier search-based unit test generation work.
closest_cited_work.quote: using a genetic algorithm in the style of earlier work [1]
